results.corrected_claim: `.presentationBackground(.clear)` does not show glass. It replaces the sheet's system Liquid Glass background with a fully transparent one, so the presenter shows through with no material. Declaration: `nonisolated func presentationBackground<S>(_ style: S) -> some View where S : ShapeStyle`. Availability: iOS 16.4, iPadOS 16.4, Mac Catalyst 16.4, macOS 13.3, tvOS 16.4, visionOS 1.0, watchOS 9.4; not deprecated. Abstract: 'Sets the presentation background of the enclosing sheet using a shape style.' A presentation background 'Automatically fills the entire presentation' and 'Allows views behind the presentation to show through translucent styles on supported platforms.' WWDC25-323: 'On iOS 26, partial height sheets are inset by default with a Liquid Glass background.' and 'If you've used the presentationBackground modifier to apply a custom background to your sheets, consider removing that and let the new material shine.' To keep the glass, remove presentationBackground and use a partial-height detent. The snippet's detents are `.large` only, and at full height the system background turns opaque anyway: 'When transitioning to a full height sheet, the glass background gradually transitions, becoming opaque and anchoring to the edge of the screen.'
results.notes: Sources checked: [apple-video] WWDC25-323 transcript, quotes verified verbatim. [apple-doc] https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/swiftui/view/presentationbackground(_:).json, with declaration, raw platforms JSON (no deprecatedAt), abstract and both bullets verified. [apple-other] The Adopting Liquid Glass article says: 'When a half sheet expands to full height, it transitions to a more opaque appearance to help maintain focus on the task.' The 'no glass at all' conclusion is inferred: the doc says the modifier 'Sets the presentation background', and WWDC's advice implies a custom background displaces the new material. Both sources point the same way, but neither states it in so many words. 'Hurts legibility' is the finding's own judgment, not an Apple statement. macOS caveat from the doc: 'Sheet presentations on macOS do not support translucency or transparency — the background is always opaque.' Outside this finding, the same snippet (lines 82-87) has another bug. It pairs `.presentationDetents([.large])` with `.presentationBackgroundInteraction(.enabled(upThrough: .medium))`. Apple's doc for enabled(upThrough:) says: 'At detents larger than the one you specify, SwiftUI disables interaction.' With only `.large`, interaction is never enabled, so the heading 'Tall sheet that doesn't dim background' isn't achieved either.

results.corrected_claim: Declaration: `nonisolated func scrollContentBackground(_ visibility: Visibility) -> some View`. Availability: iOS 16.0, iPadOS 16.0, Mac Catalyst 16.0, macOS 13.0, visionOS 1.0, watchOS 9.0; not available on tvOS. It 'Specifies the visibility of the background for scrollable views within this view.' Apple's only example hides 'the standard system background of the List'. The macOS 15 note says: 'List and Form have the seamless appearance by default, configurable by hiding the scroll background. ScrollView can become seamless by making the background visible.' So a ScrollView's scroll background is off by default. Applying `.hidden` to the plain ScrollView at glass-modal-sheet.md:42 has no documented effect, and the comment 'so glass shows through scrollables' does not apply there. The modifier is the right tool when sheet content is a List or Form. 01-api-reference.md:438 applies it to InfoView, whose contents are not shown, so that line is not demonstrably wrong.
results.notes: Sources checked: [apple-doc] declaration, platform list (tvOS absent), abstract and the List example all verified verbatim. Where the finding goes beyond the docs: (1) No Apple page says an iOS ScrollView has no background; the ScrollView page doesn't mention backgrounds at all. 'Does nothing' on iOS is an inference: it fits the docs but they don't state it. (2) The TextEditor page doesn't mention scrollContentBackground or any background, so '(and TextEditor)' is not Apple-documented. (3) Calling line 60 and api-reference:438 factually wrong overreaches. Line 60 is a general statement that holds for List and Form, and the skill's own line 99 already treats Form as having a default backing. Suggested fix: remove the modifier from the ScrollView example, or keep it only where the sheet content is a List or Form. [secondary; seen only as a search snippet, the page was unreachable] A nilcoalescing.com article reportedly says Form and List have opaque backgrounds that cover the sheet glass, and recommends `.scrollContentBackground(.hidden)` on the Form.

results.corrected_claim: Declaration: `nonisolated func containerBackground<S>(_ style: S, for container: ContainerBackgroundPlacement) -> some View where S : ShapeStyle`. Availability: iOS 17.0, iPadOS 17.0, Mac Catalyst 17.0, macOS 14.0, tvOS 17.0, visionOS 1.0, watchOS 10.0. It 'Sets the container background of the enclosing container.' `static let navigation: ContainerBackgroundPlacement` is 'A background placement inside a NavigationStack or NavigationSplitView', and Apple lists it only for iOS 18.0, iPadOS 18.0, Mac Catalyst 18.0 and watchOS 10.0. It sets the background of the navigation container's content, not of the nav bar, and it only affects a navigation container that encloses the modified view. Apple's example puts it on the NavigationLink destination content inside the NavigationStack. In 01-api-reference.md:439 it is applied to InfoView at the sheet root, and the snippet shows no enclosing NavigationStack. No Apple doc says it 'lets the nav-bar glass blend with the sheet's glass'. ContainerBackgroundPlacement has no member for sheets or presentations.
results.notes: Sources checked: [apple-doc] containerbackground(_:for:).json, containerbackgroundplacement.json and containerbackgroundplacement/navigation.json, all verified verbatim. The placement members are navigation, tabView, widget, subscriptionStore, subscriptionStoreFullHeight, subscriptionStoreHeader, navigationSplitView and window; none mention sheets. The finding's 'must be applied inside the NavigationStack' is supported by the doc's 'enclosing container' wording and the .navigation abstract. [secondary] Apple Developer Forums thread 793166 (July 2025, iOS 26 beta) was answered by the original poster, not an Apple engineer. It reports that screens pushed inside a sheet's NavigationStack turn opaque, and that putting `.containerBackground(Color.clear, for: .navigation)` on the pushed destination view keeps the sheet's glass visible. That suggests an accurate rewrite: apply the modifier to views inside the stack so the sheet's glass shows through. It is not Apple guidance.

results.corrected_claim: `toolbarBackground(_ visibility: Visibility, for bars: ToolbarPlacement...)`, introduced in iOS 16.0, has doc metadata deprecatedAt '27.2' and renamed 'toolbarBackgroundVisibility(_:for:)' on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS and watchOS. The visionOS entry has neither field. Replacement: `nonisolated func toolbarBackgroundVisibility(_ visibility: Visibility, for bars: ToolbarPlacement...) -> some View`, available on iOS 18.0, iPadOS 18.0, Mac Catalyst 18.0, macOS 15.0, tvOS 18.0, visionOS 2.0, watchOS 11.0. Use `.toolbarBackgroundVisibility(.hidden, for: .navigationBar)`. No Apple doc says items 'still float as glass shapes individually' when the bar background is hidden. WWDC25-323 says toolbar items 'are placed on a Liquid Glass surface that floats above your app's content' and 'are automatically grouped', which contradicts 'individually'.
results.notes: Sources checked: [apple-doc] raw platforms JSON verified for both symbols. 'deprecated: false' does not mean the overload isn't deprecated. In swift-docc's render schema (AvailabilityRenderMetadataItem.swift), the JSON key 'deprecated' maps to unconditionallyDeprecated, while 'deprecatedAt' is 'The version of the platform SDK deprecating the symbol'. [apple-other] 27.2 is the current beta: the iOS & iPadOS release-notes index lists 'iOS & iPadOS 27.2 Beta 3 Release Notes', and that page says 'The SDK comes bundled with Xcode 27.2.' Its sections include none for SwiftUI, and the SwiftUI Updates page (September and June 2026) doesn't mention this deprecation either. So the warning only appears when building with the 27.2 SDK, and the rename is safe for an iOS 26+ skill now. Apple docs don't say what hiding the nav-bar background does under iOS 26's scroll edge effect. The documented iOS 26 control for that effect is `scrollEdgeEffectHidden(_:for:)` (iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS and watchOS 26.0).

results.corrected_claim: `toolbar(_ visibility: Visibility, for bars: ToolbarPlacement...)`, introduced in iOS 16.0, has doc metadata deprecatedAt '27.2' and renamed 'toolbarVisibility(_:for:)' on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS and watchOS. The visionOS entry has no deprecatedAt and no renamed field. Replacement: `nonisolated func toolbarVisibility(_ visibility: Visibility, for bars: ToolbarPlacement...) -> some View`, available on iOS 18.0, iPadOS 18.0, Mac Catalyst 18.0, macOS 15.0, tvOS 18.0, visionOS 2.0, watchOS 11.0. Use `.toolbarVisibility(.hidden, for: .tabBar)`.
results.notes: Sources checked: [apple-doc] raw platforms JSON verified for both symbols. As in finding 11, 'deprecated: false' is the unconditional-deprecation flag, not a sign the method is current, and 27.2 is in beta (per the 27.2 Beta 3 release notes). Outside this finding, the same lines (glass-tab-bar.md:75-81) have a separate problem. The heading says 'within a deep navigation' and the comment says 'hides only within this stack', but the modifier is on the stack's root view, HomeView. Apple only says 'The preferred visibility flows up to the nearest container that renders a bar' and 'Depending on the specified bars, the requested visibility may not be able to be fulfilled.' The per-stack scoping in the comment isn't documented, and as written the example would hide the tab bar on that tab's root screen. Showing it on a pushed destination would match the heading.

results.corrected_claim: On iPhone, toolbar search sits in the bottom toolbar, not the nav bar. That applies to `.searchable` in a NavigationStack with or without `.searchToolbarBehavior(.minimize)`; for automatic placement Apple says 'In iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, the search field appears in the toolbar.' WWDC25-323: 'Search in the toolbar places the field at the bottom of the screen, within easy reach. And on iPad and Mac, it appears in the top-trailing position of the toolbar.' Declaration: `nonisolated func searchToolbarBehavior(_ behavior: SearchToolbarBehavior) -> some View`, available on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS 26.0. Its doc says: 'On iPhone, the search field in the bottom toolbar can be configured to appear as a button-like control when inactive.' SearchToolbarBehavior has two members: `automatic` and `minimize` ('A search toolbar behavior that prefers rendering a search field as a button-like control'). The system may also minimize the field on its own 'Depending on device size, number of toolbar buttons, and other factors'. The HIG does allow search 'in a top toolbar, also called a navigation bar, where it appears as a toolbar button', but it says 'Place search at the bottom if there’s room' and 'Place search at the top when itʼs important to defer to content at the bottom of the screen, or thereʼs no bottom toolbar.'
results.notes: Sources checked, all quotes verified verbatim: [apple-video] WWDC25-323 transcript; [apple-doc] searchtoolbarbehavior(_:).json and searchtoolbarbehavior.json; [apple-other] HIG search-fields.json. The Adopting Liquid Glass article's image alt text also reads 'A graphic of an iPhone showing search in a toolbar at the bottom of the screen' and 'A graphic of an iPad showing search in a toolbar in the upper trailing corner.' Nuance: 'lives in the nav bar' is accurate for iPad and Mac, and for the HIG's top-toolbar variant, and 'collapses to an icon' matches `.minimize`. So the fix should make the text platform-specific rather than just delete 'nav bar'. Caution for whoever applies the fix: Apple's own sample on the searchToolbarBehavior page reads `.searchable($searchText)` and `.searchToolbarBehavior(.minimized)`. Neither matches the declared API: the member is `minimize`, and searchable takes a `text:` label. The skill's `.minimize` is correct and should not be changed to `.minimized`. The docs I checked don't say where search goes on iPhone when the stack sits inside a TabView without a search tab. Related claim outside this finding: glass-tab-bar.md:85 says the search tab surfaces the field 'at the top of the screen'. WWDC25-323 instead says that on iPhone 'a search field takes the place of the tab bar', and on iPad and Mac it 'appears centered above your apps browsing suggestions'. The HIG's 'Standard tab' style describes 'a search landing page with a search field at the top'.
